subject: Computer Networking
title: SQL Injection
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on SQL Injection.

hook.text: A hacker types code into a login form. The server runs it as a database command. The entire database is exposed.

buildup.text: SQL injection happens when user input is inserted directly into database queries without sanitization.

discovery.text: An attacker adds SQL commands in a form field. The server blindly executes them against the database.

twist.text: It's one of the oldest web attacks and still appears in OWASP's Top 10 every year. Easy to prevent, yet widespread.

climax.text: Parameterized queries and prepared statements prevent it completely. Never concatenate user input into SQL.

punchline.text: SQL injection is trivially preventable. Yet it still works.

quiz.question: How is SQL injection prevented?
options: By using parameterized queries instead of string concatenation

details.summary: SQL injection inserts malicious SQL code into application inputs that get included in database queries. A successful attack can read, modify, or delete database contents, bypass authentication, or execute operating system commands. It remains one of the most common and dangerous web vulnerabilities.
details.whyItMatters: SQL injection can give attackers complete control of an application's database. Despite being well-understood for decades, it remains prevalent because developers continue writing vulnerable code.
takeaways: Malicious SQL is injected through unsanitized user inputs
Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection completely
WAFs provide additional defense but are not a substitute for secure code

faq.question: How do parameterized queries prevent SQL injection?
faq.answer: Parameterized queries separate SQL code from user data by sending them to the database separately. The database engine treats parameters strictly as data values, never as executable SQL. Even if a user inputs malicious SQL code, it is treated as a literal string, not a command.

faq.question: Can SQL injection affect modern applications?
faq.answer: Yes. Any application that constructs SQL queries using string concatenation with user input is vulnerable. ORMs generally protect against injection but raw queries or improperly used ORM features can still be vulnerable. Regular code review and automated scanning help catch these issues.
